revisionNote: The three implicit-pacing requests specify ordered events without relative duration guidance, following review of the first live run.

cases.title: Spoken line, listener reaction and visual reveal

workspace.creativeRequest: Exactly four shots, in this order: Shot 1 shows Mara and Eli beside a closed cupboard. In Shot 2 Mara says the supplied sentence. In Shot 3 Eli silently reacts and turns toward the cupboard. In Shot 4 Mara opens it and reveals a small kitten asleep inside. No additional speech.
workspace.dialogue: Mara: "I think your missing visitor has been here all morning."

workspace.creativeRequest: Exactly three shots, in this order: Shot 1 shows a loose shopping trolley begin rolling down a gentle slope. In Shot 2 a nearby worker notices it, runs several steps, catches the handle and stops it safely. In Shot 3 the worker sees that the eggs in the trolley are intact and reacts with relief. No dialogue or extra hazards.

cases.title: Dawn mist, falling dew, ripple and horizon

workspace.creativeRequest: Exactly four shots, in this order, on an empty lakeside jetty at dawn: Shot 1 shows mist moving over the jetty and water. Shot 2 shows a bead of dew detach from the railing and fall. Shot 3 shows the resulting ripple expanding across the water. Shot 4 shows the dawn horizon. No people or dialogue.

cases.title: Four comparable actions with a steady regular rhythm

workspace.creativeRequest: Exactly four shots in a steady rhythmic sequence: a hand sets down a red cup, then a blue cup, then a green cup, then a yellow cup. Each shot contains the same simple placing action, comparable framing and a brief settled hold. Cut with the same recurring musical pulse; no action needs special emphasis or extra time. No dialogue.

cases.title: User-authored opening hold and door-slam cut

workspace.creativeRequest: Exactly three shots. Hold the opening shot until exactly 4 seconds, looking at a quiet doorway; start Shot 2 at 4 seconds, showing a hand pulling the door shut. Cut when the door slams at exactly 6 seconds; start Shot 3 at 6 seconds on the startled cat beside the door, then let it settle for the rest of the clip. Preserve those exact cut times. No dialogue.
